id: title:Gilbert09:accept a repository pasted as a github url

observations.behavior: Adds a helper to normalize repository identifiers by stripping trailing .git and converting URLs like https://github.com/owner/repo.git or git@github.com:owner/repo.git into canonical owner/repo form.
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents warehouse ingestion failures caused by users entering full clone URLs or bare host paths; PostHog's warehouse connector would otherwise reject these valid inputs or create duplicate tables.

observations.behavior: Replaces manual strip/lowercasing of repository names in the effective_repositories configuration parser with the new normalization function.
observations.posthog_connection: Ensures that regardless of how a user specifies repositories in warehouse settings, they are consistently resolved before downstream processing, avoiding mismatches between config and actual GitHub API calls.

observations.behavior: Adds test coverage asserting that both URL-formatted and short-form repository entries resolve to identical storage keys.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against silent duplication when warehouse sources ingest multiple representations of the same repository.

observations.limitations: Only P1 chunk provided. No changes shown for other warehouse connectors, shared identity resolution, or end-to-end integration tests beyond this module. Tier 3 requires broader systemic demonstration across components.

review.limitations: Only P1 chunk provided. No changes shown for other warehouse connectors, shared identity resolution, or end-to-end integration tests beyond this module. Tier 3 requires broader systemic demonstration across components.
review.reason: The patch demonstrates a bounded correctness improvement: it normalizes repository identifiers uniformly within the GitHub warehouse source connector, including credential validation and ingestion parsing. This reduces misconfiguration and duplicate-table risks without changing PostHog's core query engine or person identity model. Tests support the behavior but do not establish wider adoption or cross-component dependency.
review.posthog_relevance: Warehouse ingestion is an optional data-source capability; fixing its configuration robustness helps reliability and usability for customers using GitHub as their warehouse backend, though it does not affect all users.
review.uncertainty: Assessment relies solely on P1 chunk; no access to complete PR or related hunks in other warehouse connectors.
